solution 10[edit]

Extend lines AB and CD until they intersect. Calling that point E, you can find out that triangle EBC is equilateral because the angles at B and C are 60 degrees. Assume that side BC=a, then BE and CE are also equal to a. Assuming that AE=x, then DE must also be x because triangle AED is equilateral. This also means that AD=x. Since CD=CE-DE, we have CD=a-x. Similarly, AB=a-x because AB=CD. This means the perimeter of the trapezoid ABCD is a+(a-x)+(a-x)+x. The problem tells us that the perimeter is 30 so we get the equation 3a-x=30. Adding x and dividing by 3 you get a=10-x/3. Since x is a side length, it must be an integer. That means x can any integer between 0 and 30 exclusive. Side length a must also be an integer, that means x must be a multiple of 3. So x can be 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27. From the image given to us, we see that BC=a is greater than AD=x. That means x can't be greater than or equal to 15 because that would cause x to be greater than a. This leaves us with 4 values of x which are 3,6,9,12. That means there are 4 non-congruent trapezoids that satisfy those conditions. This means the answer is .
